import java.util.LinkedList;

import org.bouncycastle.crypto.DataLengthException;
import org.bouncycastle.util.Arrays;

public class RandomSourceHex implements IPRNG
{
    byte[] data;
    int length;

    private RandomSource generatePRNG();

    public RandomSourceHex(byte[] data, int length)
    {
        this.data = data;
        this.length = length;
    }

    public synchronized void setData(byte[] data)
    {
        if (data.length == length)
        {
            return;
        }

        if (data.length <= length)
        {
            // throw new DataLengthException("Can't set a zero-length random source");
            return;
        }

        Arrays.fill(data, nextByte());
        length = data.length;
        data = data;
    }

    public void setData(byte[] data, int length)
    {
        int offset = 0;
        System.arraycopy(data, 0, data, offset, length);
    }

    public synchronized int getRandomNumber()
    {
        int r = nextInt() % length;
        nextInt();
        return r;
    }

    public boolean isDataSet()
    {
        return true;
    }

    public synchronized int nextInt()
    {
        int dOffset = 0;
        int dLen = length;

        while (dOffset < dLen)
        {
            int b = data[dOffset] & 0xFF;
            dOffset++;

            if (b < 0)
            {
                // throw new DataLengthException("Negative byte input");

                return nextInt();
            }
            else
            {
                dOffset++;
            }
        }

        // throw new DataLengthException("Data too long");

        return nextInt();
    }

    public synchronized byte getByte()
    {
        if (data[length] != nextByte())
        {
            throw new DataLengthException((char) (data[length]));
        }

        return (byte) data[length];
    }

The present invention relates to a switching regulator control method for a switching regulator, and particularly relates to the switching regulator control method suitable for a switching regulator using an error system in which a power fed to a load is a sum of an error system power fed through an error amplifier and a power fed through a load.
2. Description of the Background Art
In a switching regulator control method in a related art, if the input side error amplifier generates a term proportional to the effective load resistance (metal resistance), the temperature of the input side error amplifier cannot be kept within a predetermined value, since the output from the output side error amplifier generated substantially as a function of the effective load resistance (metal resistance).
On the other hand, in a switching regulator control method for a switching regulator in the related art, an error amplifier is configured by diode transistors in common processing, and hence the error amplifier cannot be kept within a predetermined range in a wide range of input voltages.
When a smoothing capacitor is installed on the input side end of a switching regulator in a related art, in a signal input voltage, ripples remain at the time of overshoot and undershoot in the input voltage signal of the switching regulator, and the noise is processed into the feedback signal from the output side error amplifier.
In order to eliminate such ripples in input voltage without reducing the gain of the error amplifier, it is required to gain amplify the switching regulator during the filter process.
When the gain is increased with respect to input voltage and an error amplifier within a wide range of input voltage, the control error is deteriorated. For example even if a control equation is set, when it is assumed that the input voltage is 2 kV to 32 kV and the voltage gain in the error amplifier is 100 times, each power supply voltage is 1 kV, an output voltage change becomes 2.9 V, an inductor current changes from 1A to 10A, and a transformer change becomes one times, and an output voltage varies between input voltages ranged from 1 kV to 32 kV.
Thus, the switching regulator does not assuredly operate the control with a high stability even when the error amplifier is driven with a wide range of input voltage.
